text:
Braeden Bowman is an undrafted winger who worked his way up through Henderson and has stuck in Vegas's bottom six, about 13 minutes a night. His week had both sides of that role: a five-minute major and game misconduct for an elbow on Matthew Poitras in Boston on Nov. 2, with no further action from the league, and then a third-period equalizer in Detroit three nights later that The Athletic's Jesse Granger called a heck of a shot, a little drag to change the angle before he beat the goalie's glove.

He has seven points in 19 games, and our numbers say he's been short-changed. The Golden Knights have scored 6.0 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which costs a depth player assists. His own finishing (four goals on 4.13 expected) is about right. The worry is the five-on-five process: Vegas is a lot worse at controlling play with him out there. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him as a dump-in winger who finishes passes from the slot; Evolving-Hockey had him 195th of 401 forwards last season. Our projection: around 14 goals.
